zh.title: 相机怎么选：先看约束，不看品牌
zh.summary: 先写你拍什么、在哪拍、给谁看、能背多重，再选机身。参数表不能替你做决定。

zh.title: 录音入门：话筒位置比设备贵更重要
zh.summary: 同一支便宜话筒，放在离嘴 20 厘米的位置，通常比一万元设备放在机顶更好。

zh.title: 素材管理：当天备份，命名可查
zh.summary: 拍摄结束前做完备份，文件名带日期、场次、机位。找不到的素材等于没拍。

zh.title: 第一次开机，先把这 6 件事写下来
zh.summary: 第一次拍片，现场最容易乱的就是时间、地点、谁负责、先拍什么、备用方案和收工标准。写在一页纸上，比脑子里记靠谱。

zh.title: 发布前 12 项检查：别在最后一小时翻车
zh.summary: 授权、技术、发布三组检查。每一项都能在十分钟内查完，别等到上传后才看到黑帧和错字。

zh.title: 预算里留 10%，给意外留个座位
zh.summary: 天气、场地超时、补拍、临时加人，这四件事几乎每次都会发生。预算表上没有它们，超支就会从别的地方偷。

zh.title: 场地：开拍前先问清五件事
zh.summary: 场地不是“看起来合适”就能拍。谁有权答应、邻居会不会投诉、电从哪来、声音收不收得住、出了问题谁赔，五件事任何一件没问清，现场都可能停。

zh.title: 通告单：一张纸，把今天说清
zh.summary: 通告单不是形式。它决定谁几点到、去哪、带什么、找谁。写不清，现场的电话就会比拍摄还忙。

zh.title: 预算表：把钱分成四块
zh.summary: 预算不是一列数字，是四块怎么分：必须花的、会上镜的、能替换的、会爆的。先保片子能拍完，再谈好看。

zh.title: 拍摄日程：把剧本拆成条
zh.summary: 排期不是把场景按顺序填进日历。先按地点和人物拆条，再按天分组；同一天只搬一次家，演员只来一次。日程保护的不是进度，是表演。

zh.title: 选人：先站得住，再看戏
zh.summary: 选演员不是找最会演的，是找最适合这段关系的人。先看外形和声音是否成立，再看两个人站在一起有没有事，最后才看台词。试读给一个动作，不给一段独白。

zh.title: 交付：别在最后导错文件
zh.summary: 交付不是点导出。先问平台要什么：比例、分辨率、帧率、码率、色彩、声道、文件名。做一个能重复的模板，交付前自己从头播一遍。

zh.title: 提案：先让人看见片子
zh.summary: 提案不是把剧本换成漂亮话，是让客户在开机前看见片子的样子、语气和边界。

zh.title: 开机曝光检查：波形、斑马、假色
zh.summary: 开机曝光检查按顺序：波形看分布、斑马看高光、伪色看人脸；三个都过再开拍。

zh.title: ND 计算：大光圈白天怎么曝光
zh.summary: ND 计算先定快门和光圈，再算需要减几档；凭感觉换滤镜，十次有九次过暗。

zh.title: 存储时长计算器：卡能录多久
zh.summary: 存储计算器按码率、时长和备份份数算空间；卡能录多久，不要靠相机剩余时间。

zh.title: 电影机：传感器、卡口、录制
zh.summary: 电影机先看传感器、卡口和录制格式；名字和外形不决定它能不能拍你的项目。

zh.title: 微单拍视频：过热、果冻、裁切
zh.summary: 微单拍视频先查三件事：会不会过热、果冻有多明显、录视频时裁不裁画幅。

zh.title: 定焦镜头：先走动，再变焦
zh.summary: 定焦不是不能变焦，它逼你走近、退后、换机位；这通常比拧变焦环更有用。

zh.title: 变焦镜头：方便与画质
zh.summary: 变焦镜头省时间，但要在重量、光圈和画质之间付账；先问今天最缺哪一样。

zh.title: 变形宽银幕：炫光与畸变
zh.summary: 变形宽银幕不是把画面上下裁掉；它压缩横向、再还原，所以有椭圆光斑和独特畸变。

zh.title: 增光减焦：画幅与光圈
zh.summary: 增光减焦把全画幅镜头压到小画幅机身上，视角变宽、光圈约快一档，但边缘可能变软。

zh.title: 遮光斗：滤镜与漏光
zh.summary: 遮光斗先挡杂光，再装滤镜；便宜的遮光斗可能漏光，反而毁画面。

zh.title: 跟焦器：单手能跟
zh.summary: 跟焦器让焦点变化有刻度、有手感；自动对焦在暗处和快速运动时不一定靠得住。

zh.title: LED 面板灯：显色与亮度
zh.summary: LED 面板灯先看显色指数和实际亮度，不看包装上的瓦数；人脸发绿就是显色不对。

zh.title: COB 灯：一盏灯加柔光箱
zh.summary: COB 灯是裸光源，必须配柔光箱或灯笼；裸着照人脸，影子会硬得没法看。

zh.title: 柔光箱：尺寸决定柔度
zh.summary: 柔光箱越大、越近，光越柔；换灯不如先把柔光箱靠近人物。

zh.title: 反光板：五合一怎么用
zh.summary: 反光板五合一不是五种风格，是五种补光强度；先用白色，别一上来就银面。

zh.title: 灯光色纸：CTO、CTB、ND
zh.summary: 灯光色纸先分清 CTO、CTB、ND：一个加暖、一个加冷、一个减亮；贴错会改掉整个现场。

zh.title: 实用灯泡：色温与调光
zh.summary: 实用灯泡要能调色温和亮度，否则画面里的灯只能当道具，不能当光源。

zh.title: 灯架与沙袋：安全第一
zh.summary: 灯架先放沙袋，再升灯；一根没配重的灯架，倒下来比灯贵。

zh.title: 枪麦：指向性与离轴
zh.summary: 枪麦是指向性工具，离得远就只能收环境；先靠近，再谈降噪。

zh.title: 无线领夹系统：频段与备份
zh.summary: 无线领夹先查频段和干扰，再录一条备用轨；现场没有第二次机会。

zh.title: 录音机：32-bit 浮点
zh.summary: 32-bit 浮点录音能救回削波，但救不回被风吞掉的对白；麦克风和位置还是第一位。

zh.title: 监听耳机：闭耳与漏音
zh.summary: 监听耳机要封闭、贴合、不美化；用消费耳机监听，等于闭眼调色。

zh.title: 时间码：多机同步
zh.summary: 时间码让多机位和录音机在后期的第一分钟就对上；没有它，合板要靠运气。

zh.title: 音频接口：输入与增益
zh.summary: 音频接口先看输入数量、增益范围和底噪；接口再贵，增益不够也录不了小声。

zh.title: 三脚架：云台与承重
zh.summary: 三脚架先看承重和云台，不看最大高度；相机加镜头加配件，往往比标称重。

zh.title: 液压云台：三脚架怎么跟
zh.summary: 液压云台的价值在阻尼：起停要顺，不能一碰就飞。

zh.title: 稳定器：平衡与步伐
zh.summary: 稳定器先调平再开机；电机一直在救不平衡，画面就会抖，电池也撑不住。

zh.title: 滑轨：起停与声音
zh.summary: 滑轨最容易暴露起停：先慢起、匀走、缓停，别让轮子声进对白。

zh.title: 监视器：亮度、波形、LUT
zh.summary: 现场监视器先看亮度、波形和 LUT；屏幕好看不代表素材对。

zh.title: 无线图传：延迟与干扰
zh.summary: 无线图传先测延迟和干扰，再决定给导演还是给跟焦；信号断了，现场就会停。

zh.title: 视频助理：现场回放
zh.summary: 视频助理负责回放、标记和备份；导演能立刻看到刚才那条，拍摄速度会快很多.

zh.title: 示波器监视：曝光与色彩
zh.summary: 带示波器的监视器能同时看曝光和色彩；只看直方图，会漏掉肤色偏移。

zh.title: CFexpress 卡：速度与发热
zh.summary: CFexpress 卡先看持续写入和发热，不看峰值；拍长条时，热降速比容量更致命。

zh.title: SSD RAID：剪辑阵列
zh.summary: SSD RAID 是剪辑工作盘，不是归档；阵列一坏，重建比备份更贵。

zh.title: NAS：团队共享
zh.summary: NAS 让全组共享素材，但必须先定命名、权限和回收站规则；否则共享等于互相覆盖。

zh.title: LTO 归档：长期冷备
zh.summary: LTO 适合长期冷备，不适合当天剪辑；先算恢复时间，再算每 TB 成本。

zh.title: 剪辑软件怎么选：项目先定
zh.summary: 剪辑软件按项目选：团队协作、代理、调色、字幕、交付，各有所长；别按教程数量选。

zh.title: 达芬奇节点：节点不是滤镜
zh.summary: 节点不是滤镜叠叠乐；每个节点只做一件事，关掉它就能看出它干了什么。

zh.title: AI 视频工具：先看可控性
zh.summary: AI 视频工具先看可控性：能不能锁角色、锁镜头、锁时长；只看样片会被骗。

zh.title: AI 音频工具：授权与音质
zh.summary: AI 音频工具先查授权和音质，再看功能；克隆声音的授权范围比音色重要。

zh.title: 动画软件：2D、3D、定格
zh.summary: 动画软件按工序选：2D 看绘图和合成，3D 看绑定和渲染，定格看拍摄控制；一个软件不可能全包。

zh.title: 云渲染：成本与传输
zh.summary: 云渲染先算上传时间和出图成本；素材太大，上传比渲染更慢。

zh.title: 相机黑平衡：别把噪点当风格
zh.summary: 相机黑平衡按机器要求做，别把噪点当风格；暗部干净，后期才有空间。

zh.title: 灰卡白平衡：混合光怎么对
zh.summary: 灰卡白平衡解决混合光下的中性；先把灰卡放到主体位置，再读。

zh.title: 跟焦练习：三步走
zh.summary: 跟焦练习三步：先做标记、盯住演员的胸口、呼吸别跟着手抖。

zh.title: 手持支撑：三个接触点
zh.summary: 手持支撑找三个接触点：胸口、肩膀、手肘；三点稳定，画面才不像地震。

zh.title: 稳定器调平：开机前五分钟
zh.summary: 稳定器调平按三轴依次做，每次锁轴再调下一轴；开机前五分钟，省现场半小时。

zh.title: 滑轨起停：让运动有头尾
zh.summary: 滑轨镜头要有头、身、尾：起幅停半秒、过程匀、落幅停半秒。

zh.title: 吊杆移动：跟着台词走
zh.summary: 吊杆跟着演员胸口走，不跟着嘴；嘴会转，胸口不会突然消失。

zh.title: 领夹藏麦：衣领、头发、胶带
zh.summary: 领夹藏麦先试衣领，再试头发，最后用医用胶带固定；每换一件衣服都要重藏。

zh.title: 双系统合板：拍手与时间码
zh.summary: 双系统合板先拍手，再对时间码；两条都对上，后期才不用逐条听。

zh.title: 环境音录制：三十秒规则
zh.summary: 每个场景录三十秒环境声，全组安静；没有它，剪对话会像在真空里。

zh.title: 单灯人像：先有方向
zh.summary: 单灯人像先定方向：45 度、侧光还是逆光；方向对了，再谈柔硬和亮度。

zh.title: 窗光补光：反光板位置
zh.summary: 窗光补光把反光板放在阴影侧，别放在窗边；反光板是补暗，不是加亮。

zh.title: 夜景实用光：曝光平衡
zh.summary: 夜景实用光先让画面里的灯成立，再用小灯补人脸；两者亮度差太多，就会假。

zh.title: 色卡拍摄：后期对色
zh.summary: 色卡在场景光下拍一张，后期才有基准；开机后补拍，光已经变了。

zh.title: 代理生成：剪辑不卡
zh.summary: 代理按时间线和交付分辨率生成，别用完整分辨率硬剪；代理不对，字幕和构图会错。

zh.title: 多机位同步：时间码与手动
zh.summary: 多机位同步先对时间码，再用拍手兜底；两样都做，剪辑才敢切。

zh.title: SRT 字幕：编码、时间轴、标点
zh.summary: SRT 字幕先保 UTF-8 编码、时间轴和标点；编码错了，平台会显示乱码。

zh.title: H.264 导出：码率与兼容
zh.summary: H.264 导出先定平台和码率，再选两遍编码；码率太低，运动画面先烂。

zh.title: ProRes 导出：归档与交付
zh.summary: ProRes 用于归档和再调色，不是给所有平台直接上传；文件大，但能再改。

zh.title: 3-2-1 备份：当天做完
zh.summary: 3-2-1 备份当天做完：三份、两种介质、一份异地；拖到明天，素材就可能没了。

zh.title: 恢复演练：随机抽一个文件
zh.summary: 恢复演练随机抽一个文件，从备份打开；打不开的备份等于没有。

zh.title: 素材车：现场拷卡与命名
zh.summary: 素材车现场拷卡、校验、命名、备份；回机房再整理，时间会翻倍。

zh.title: ND 计算器：换滤镜不靠猜
zh.summary: ND 计算器把快门、光圈、ISO 和目标曝光放进同一个公式；换滤镜前先算。

zh.title: 景深计算器：距离与光圈
zh.summary: 景深计算器先看主体距离，再看光圈和焦段；距离一变，景深全变。

zh.title: 码率体积计算器：文件多大
zh.summary: 码率计算器按分钟和 Mbps 算文件体积；交付前先知道硬盘够不够。

zh.title: 预算计算器：四块怎么分
zh.summary: 预算计算器把制作费分成四块：人、设备、场地、后期；每块留 10% 缓冲。

zh.title: 字幕 CPS 计算器：读得完吗
zh.summary: 字幕 CPS 计算器看每秒字符数；超过阅读速度，观众会暂停，片子就断了。

zh.title: 画幅比计算器：裁切与安全区
zh.summary: 画幅比计算器先算裁切后的有效像素，再定安全区；竖屏不是横屏两边裁掉。

zh.title: 购买相机：先定预算，再定机身
zh.summary: 预算有限时，机身不是第一优先级。先确认你缺的是暗光、自动对焦、10-bit、还是收音；买错机身，后面每一件配件都要跟着换。

zh.title: 租相机：保险、押金、检查
zh.summary: 租相机先买保险、交押金、当面检查；划痕和坏点拍视频留证。

zh.title: 先买镜头：焦段、光圈与呼吸
zh.summary: 镜头决定画面的一半，而且比机身保值。先买一支能覆盖 70% 场景的焦段，再买第二支；不要一开始凑三支便宜变焦。

zh.title: 先买录音：麦克风、底噪与增益
zh.summary: 观众能忍画面普通，忍不了声音听不清。预算有限时，先把钱放在麦克风和录音机，而不是第二支镜头。

zh.title: 购买灯光套装：先买柔，再买亮
zh.summary: 第一套灯不是最亮的，是最容易控制肤色和阴影的。柔光面积、色温一致、可调功率，比峰值亮度更重要。

zh.title: 购买项目存储：速度、容量与备份
zh.summary: 存储不是“越大越好”，是“拍摄不断、拷回不丢、项目结束还能找得到”。先算一个项目日的真实数据量，再买盘。

zh.title: 购买监视器：亮度、色域与延迟
zh.summary: 监视器不是“外接大屏”。现场要亮到看得见、色彩要能校准、延迟要能对焦；三项任何一项不够，都还不如机头屏。

zh.title: 购买三脚架：承重、扭转与高度
zh.summary: 三脚架的标称承重不是安全线。真正决定稳定性的是脚管刚度、云台锁紧、扭转刚度和重心；风一吹就晃的架子，承重写 20kg 也没用。

zh.title: 灯光租赁：清单与损坏
zh.summary: 灯光租赁先列清单、试亮、拍损坏；少一个灯罩，现场就得多等一小时。

zh.title: 二手器材检查：快门、卡口、传感器
zh.summary: 二手器材检查快门数、卡口松动、传感器坏点；三项都过再付钱。

zh.title: 相机过热：降温与分段拍
zh.summary: 相机过热先降温、分段拍、降码率；不要用湿毛巾直接敷机身。

zh.title: 果冻效应：读速与快门
zh.summary: 果冻效应来自慢读出和快速运动；先换机器，再调快门，别只怪镜头。

zh.title: 底噪排查：从房间开始
zh.summary: 底噪排查从房间开始：关空调、关灯、换插座、换线；最后才怪麦克风。

zh.title: 导出失败排查：编码、磁盘、权限
zh.summary: 导出失败先查编码、磁盘空间、权限；三样都排除，再重建项目。

zh.title: 预算与报价：把风险写进数字
zh.summary: 预算不是成本清单，是把“会停拍的那一项”先保住。报价不是成本加 20%，是把范围、修改、授权和风险分别定价。

zh.title: 剧组管理：通告、签到、收工与责任
zh.summary: 剧组管理不是发通告，是让每个人知道今天做什么、出事找谁、什么时候能走。通告单、签到、收工报告三张纸决定项目是否可控。

zh.title: 购买电影机：别把“能拍”当成“能交”
zh.summary: 电影机的价格不只在机身：卡、电池、监看、底座、提手、线材、调色和学习都要算。先确认项目真的需要 RAW、时码、SDI 和双卡，否则一台高端视频机更划算。

zh.title: 购买变焦：齐焦、呼吸与伺服
zh.summary: 变焦的价值是“不换镜”，不是“什么都能拍”。先确认它在推拉时能保住焦点、呼吸不明显、伺服不吵；否则你买的是一支会变焦的定焦。

zh.title: 现场录音机：通道、32 位浮点与时码
zh.summary: 现场录音机的核心不是“能录几轨”，而是“断了一个通道还有没有备份、增益错了能不能救、后期能不能对时码”。

zh.title: 购买 LED 灯：亮度、频闪与供电
zh.summary: LED 的参数不只是瓦数。频闪、色温偏移、电池续航、DMX/无线控制，决定它能不能在真实拍摄现场稳定工作。

zh.title: 购买 HDR 监视器：峰值亮度不是全部
zh.summary: HDR 监看要看峰值、黑位、色域、色调映射和校准。只看“1000 nit”会买到一台高亮但高光全糊的屏。

zh.title: 购买存储卡：VPG、持续写入与发热
zh.summary: 卡的标称读取速度没有意义，持续写入才决定会不会丢帧。先看相机要求的最小持续写入，再买高一档的卡，并至少两张轮换。

zh.title: 购买液压云台：阻尼、平衡与回弹
zh.summary: 液压云台不是“能转就行”。真正的差别在俯仰阻尼是否连续、重心平衡是否够、松手后是否匀速回弹；这些决定你能否拍出稳定的摇移。

zh.title: 第一台稳定器：承重、调平与跟随
zh.summary: 稳定器不是“走路不抖”的魔法。承重余量、三轴调平、跟随手感、电池和轴锁，决定你能不能用它拍完一个镜头。

zh.title: 购买无线领夹：距离、断点与延迟
zh.summary: 无线领夹的“500 米”是空旷视距，不是商场/演唱会。先测你真实场景的断点、底噪、延迟和电池，再决定买哪一套。

zh.title: 购买时码器：漂移、同步与电池
zh.summary: 时码器不是“多机位一定需要”，但一旦需要，漂移和同步稳定性比外观重要。先测 8 小时漂移，再决定买几台。

zh.title: 购买 NAS/RAID：吞吐、重建与噪声
zh.summary: NAS 不是“插上就安全”。RAID 不是备份；重建期间性能会掉，劵盘/静音/功耗都会影响工作室。先算吞吐和重建时间。

zh.title: 购买二手器材：快门、传感器与维修
zh.summary: 二手不是“便宜”，是“把风险折成价格”。先查快门/传感器/接口/维修记录，再谈价；没有试拍和退货条款，再便宜也不要。

zh.title: 购买电池：容量、通信与安全
zh.summary: 电池不是“能开机就行”。副厂电池可能不显示电量、突然掉电、胀包；拍一天项目，电池是安全件，不是省钱件。

zh.title: 后期软件与交付：先定流程，再买工具
zh.summary: 剪辑、调色、声音、编码、审片是五个环节；先定流程，再决定订阅哪几个。不要一次买齐。

zh.title: 测试协议库：十项现场可复现测试
zh.summary: 十项测试的可复现步骤、原始记录字段和通过线；没有器材就写“未实测”，不编数字。

zh.title: 镜头视角计算器：焦距、画幅与水平视角
zh.summary: 输入传感器宽度和焦距，算出水平视角；用来判断这支镜头在室内、户外和人物近景里够不够用。

zh.title: 存储链：卡、SSD、NAS 与 LTO
zh.summary: 存储不是买一块硬盘，而是从卡到工作盘、备份盘和离线介质的一条链。

zh.title: 现场声音链：从麦克风到备份
zh.summary: 现场声音不是一支麦克风，而是麦克风、无线、录音机、备份和场记的一条链。

zh.title: 单灯套装：柔光、反光、色温
zh.summary: 一盏灯够不够，不取决于灯，而取决于柔光面积、反光位置和色温是否统一。

zh.title: 机身与镜头：一机三镜的现实组合
zh.summary: 机身决定下限，镜头决定你能拍到什么；一机三镜比一机十镜更容易拍完。

zh.title: 直播链：无线、监看、时码
zh.summary: 直播不是把相机接上电脑；无线、监看、时码和备份任何一环断了，现场就停。

zh.title: 3-2-1 备份：从卡到异地
zh.summary: 备份不是复制一份；三份、两种介质、一份异地，才算把素材从现场带回来。

zh.title: 后期工作站：NLE、代理、节点
zh.summary: 工作站不是配置单，而是 NLE、代理、缓存和节点在同一个项目里不打架。

zh.title: AI 工具链：生成、配音、渲染
zh.summary: AI 工具不是一键出片；生成、配音、渲染和人工复核必须排成一条可追溯的链。

zh.title: 器材维护：开机前、收工后与存放
zh.summary: 器材故障多数不是突然发生，是长期忽略；把检查、清洁、存放和记录做成固定动作，才不靠运气。

zh.title: 灯光安全：电、热、坠与承重
zh.summary: 灯光安全不是一句小心，是算电、算热、算坠、算承重；四件事任何一件超限，灯就不该开。

en.title: How to Choose a Camera: Constraints Before Brands
en.summary: Write what you shoot, where, for whom, and how much you can carry before choosing a body. A spec sheet cannot decide for you.

en.title: Audio Basics: Mic Position Beats Price
en.summary: A cheap mic twenty centimeters from the mouth usually beats an expensive rig mounted on the camera.

en.title: Media Management: Back Up Today, Name for Finding
en.summary: Back up before wrap. Put date, scene, and camera in the filename. Footage you cannot find was never shot.

en.title: Six Things to Write Down Before Your First Shoot Day
en.summary: First shoots fall apart around time, place, ownership, shot order, backups, and when to stop. Put all six on one page.

en.title: Twelve Checks Before Publishing: Do Not Lose the Last Hour
en.summary: Three groups of checks: rights, technical, and publishing. Each takes ten minutes; do not discover a black frame or a typo after upload.

en.title: Hold Ten Percent for the Unexpected
en.summary: Weather, overtime, reshoots, and last-minute hires happen on almost every shoot. If they are not in the budget, the overrun steals from somewhere else.

en.title: Location: Five Questions Before You Unpack
en.summary: A location is not a place that looks right. Who can say yes, who will complain, where the power comes from, what the sound does, and who pays for damage: miss one and the day stops.

en.title: Call Sheet: One Page, One Plan
en.summary: A call sheet is not paperwork. It decides who arrives when, where, with what, and whom to call. If it is vague, the set fills with phone calls and the day slows down.

en.title: Budget: Four Buckets, One Decision
en.summary: A budget is not a column of numbers. It is four buckets: what must be paid, what will be seen, what can be swapped, and what will blow up. Keep the film shootable before you make it pretty.

en.title: Stripboard: Turn the Script into Shootable Days
en.summary: Scheduling is not filling the calendar in script order. Break the script into strips by location and cast, then group them into days: one company move, one actor call. The schedule protects the performance, not just the progress.

en.title: Casting: Can They Stand in the Room Before They Can Act?
en.summary: Casting is not finding the best actor. It is finding the person who fits this relationship. Check whether the look and voice hold, then whether two people have something between them, and only then the lines. Give an action in the audition, not a monologue.

en.title: Delivery: Find the Wrong Export Before the Last Hour
en.summary: Delivery is not hitting export. Ask what the platform needs: ratio, resolution, frame rate, bitrate, color, channels, filename. Build a template you can repeat, then watch the file from start to finish.

en.title: Treatment: Make the Film Visible on Paper
en.summary: A treatment does not decorate a script; it lets the client see the film's shape, tone, and limits before the shoot.

en.title: Exposure Check: Waveform, Zebra, False Color
en.summary: Check exposure in order: waveform for distribution, zebra for highlights, false color for skin; roll only after all three.

en.title: ND Calculation: Wide Open in Daylight
en.summary: Set shutter and aperture, then calculate stops; guessing the filter leaves you dark nine times out of ten.

en.title: Storage Calculator: How Long Can You Roll?
en.summary: Calculate space from bitrate, duration, and copies; do not trust the camera's remaining-time guess.

en.title: Cine Camera: Sensor, Mount, Codec
en.summary: Cine cameras are sensor, mount, and codec first; the badge and body do not decide the job.

en.title: Mirrorless for Video: Heat, Rolling Shutter, Crop
en.summary: Check three things: overheating, rolling shutter, and whether video crops the frame.

en.title: Prime Lens: Move Your Feet
en.summary: A prime forces you to step in, back, and change position; that is often better than turning a zoom ring.

en.title: Zoom Lens: Convenience Has a Cost
en.summary: A zoom saves time but charges you in weight, aperture, and image; ask which one you can afford today.

en.title: Anamorphic: Wide Screen, Not a Crop
en.summary: Anamorphic is not a top-and-bottom crop; it squeezes the image horizontally and restores it, giving oval bokeh and specific distortion.

en.title: Speed Booster: Wider Angle, Faster Aperture
en.summary: A speed booster squeezes a full-frame lens onto a smaller sensor: wider view, about one stop faster, softer edges.

en.title: Matte Box: Filters and Stray Light
en.summary: A matte box cuts stray light before holding filters; a cheap one can leak and ruin the frame.

en.title: Follow Focus: One Hand Can Follow
en.summary: A follow focus gives marks and feel; autofocus is not reliable in darkness or fast motion.

en.title: LED Panel: CRI and Brightness
en.summary: Check CRI and real output, not wattage on the box; green skin means the color is wrong.

en.title: COB Light: One Source, One Soft Box
en.summary: A COB is a bare source; pair it with a soft box or lantern or the face gets hard shadows.

en.title: Softbox: Size Decides Softness
en.summary: Bigger and closer means softer; move the box before changing the light.

en.title: Reflector: Five Surfaces, One Job
en.summary: The five surfaces are five fill strengths, not five styles; start white, not silver.

en.title: Lighting Gel: CTO, CTB, ND
en.summary: Know CTO, CTB, and ND: warm, cool, and dim. The wrong gel changes the whole set.

en.title: Practical Bulb: Color Temperature and Dimming
en.summary: A practical must dim and shift color temperature, or it is only a prop, not a source.

en.title: Light Stand: Sandbag Everything
en.summary: Sandbag the stand before raising the light; an unweighted stand costs more than the lamp when it falls.

en.title: Shotgun Mic: Point It, Get Close
en.summary: A shotgun is directional; distance gives you room, not dialogue. Get close before denoising.

en.title: Wireless Lav: Frequency and Backup
en.summary: Check frequency and interference, and record a backup track; the set gives no second chance.

en.title: Field Recorder: 32-Bit Is Not Magic
en.summary: 32-bit float can rescue clipping, not dialogue eaten by wind; mic and placement still come first.

en.title: Monitoring Headphones: Closed, Sealed, Honest
en.summary: Monitoring headphones must be closed, sealed, and honest; consumer cans are color grading with eyes shut.

en.title: Timecode: Sync Without Guessing
en.summary: Timecode syncs cameras and recorders in the first minute of post; without it, sync is luck.

en.title: Audio Interface: Inputs and Gain
en.summary: Check input count, gain range, and noise floor; a expensive interface with low gain cannot record a whisper.

en.title: Tripod: Load and Head
en.summary: Check payload and head before max height; camera, lens, and accessories weigh more than the spec.

en.title: Fluid Head: Pan and Tilt Need Drag
en.summary: A fluid head is about drag: starts and stops must be smooth, not snappy.

en.title: Gimbal: Balance Before Power
en.summary: Balance the gimbal before powering up; motors fighting imbalance cause shake and battery drain.

en.title: Slider: Start and Stop Quietly
en.summary: A slider exposes its start and stop; ease in, move evenly, ease out, and keep wheel noise off dialogue.

en.title: Field Monitor: Brightness, Scopes, LUT
en.summary: A field monitor needs brightness, scopes, and LUT support; a pretty screen does not mean correct footage.

en.title: Wireless Video: Latency and Interference
en.summary: Test latency and interference before sending to director or focus puller; a dropped signal stops the set.

en.title: Video Assist: Playback on Set
en.summary: Video assist handles playback, marks, and backup; instant review speeds the whole set.

en.title: Scope Monitor: Exposure and Color Together
en.summary: A scope monitor shows exposure and color together; a histogram alone misses skin drift.

en.title: CFexpress: Speed and Heat
en.summary: Check sustained write and heat, not peak speed; on long takes, thermal throttling hurts before capacity.

en.title: SSD RAID: Edit Array, Not Archive
en.summary: SSD RAID is an edit workspace, not an archive; rebuilding costs more than backup.

en.title: NAS: Shared Storage, Shared Rules
en.summary: NAS shares media, so set naming, permissions, and trash rules first; otherwise sharing means overwriting.

en.title: LTO Archive: Cold, Cheap, Slow
en.summary: LTO is for cold archive, not same-day editing; calculate restore time before cost per TB.

en.title: Choosing an NLE: Start With the Project
en.summary: Choose an NLE by project needs: collaboration, proxies, grading, subtitles, delivery; not by tutorial count.

en.title: DaVinci Nodes: Nodes Are Not Filters
en.summary: Nodes are not filter stacks; one node does one job, and disabling it reveals its effect.

en.title: AI Video Tool: Controllability First
en.summary: Check controllability: can it lock character, camera, duration? Demo reels lie.

en.title: AI Audio Tool: Rights and Quality
en.summary: Check rights and audio quality before features; a cloned voice's license matters more than timbre.

en.title: Animation Software: 2D, 3D, Stop Motion
en.summary: Choose by pipeline: 2D for drawing and comp, 3D for rigging and render, stop motion for capture control.

en.title: Cloud Render: Cost and Transfer
en.summary: Calculate upload time and output cost; with big media, upload is slower than render.

en.title: Camera Black Balance: Do Not Bake Noise
en.summary: Black balance as the camera requires; do not bake noise into the look. Clean shadows give post room.

en.title: Gray Card White Balance: Mixed Light
en.summary: A gray card neutralizes mixed light; place it where the subject stands before reading.

en.title: Follow Focus Practice: Mark, Watch, Breathe
en.summary: Three steps: mark the barrel, watch the chest, and keep breathing steady.

en.title: Handheld Brace: Three Contact Points
en.summary: Find three contact points: chest, shoulder, elbow; three points stabilize the frame.

en.title: Gimbal Balance: Five Minutes Before Power
en.summary: Balance each axis with the others locked; five minutes before power saves half an hour on set.

en.title: Slider Shot: Head, Body, Tail
en.summary: A slider shot needs a head, body, and tail: hold the start, move evenly, hold the end.

en.title: Boom Swing: Follow the Chest
en.summary: Follow the chest, not the mouth; the mouth turns, the chest stays in range.

en.title: Lav Hiding: Collar, Hair, Tape
en.summary: Try collar, then hair, then medical tape; every wardrobe change needs a new hide.

en.title: Dual-System Sync: Clap and Timecode
en.summary: Clap first, then timecode; when both match, post does not have to listen to every take.

en.title: Room Tone: Thirty Seconds per Location
en.summary: Record thirty seconds of room tone per location with everyone quiet; without it, dialogue cuts sound like a vacuum.

en.title: One-Light Portrait: Direction First
en.summary: Set direction first: 45 degrees, side, or backlight; then softness and intensity.

en.title: Window Light Fill: Reflector Placement
en.summary: Place the reflector on the shadow side, not by the window; it fills shadow, not adds light.

en.title: Night Practical: Balance the Lamp
en.summary: Make the lamp in frame believable, then add a small face light; a big ratio looks fake.

en.title: Color Checker: Shoot It Before the Scene
en.summary: Shoot the chart under scene light before the take; after the first setup, the light has changed.

en.title: Proxy Creation: Match the Timeline
en.summary: Generate proxies to match timeline and delivery; full-res editing makes subtitles and framing wrong.

en.title: Multicam Sync: Timecode and Clap
en.summary: Sync timecode first, clap as backup; with both, the edit can cut confidently.

en.title: SRT Subtitles: Encoding, Timing, Punctuation
en.summary: SRT needs UTF-8, timing, and punctuation; wrong encoding shows garbage on platform.

en.title: H.264 Export: Bitrate and Compatibility
en.summary: Set platform and bitrate before two-pass encoding; low bitrate destroys motion first.

en.title: ProRes Export: Archive and Delivery
en.summary: ProRes is for archive and regrading, not direct upload everywhere; big files, but editable.

en.title: 3-2-1 Backup: Finish It Today
en.summary: Do 3-2-1 today: three copies, two media, one offsite; tomorrow the card may be gone.

en.title: Restore Test: Pick One Random File
en.summary: Restore one random file from backup; a backup that will not open does not exist.

en.title: Media Bay: Offload and Name on Set
en.summary: Offload, verify, name, and back up on set; organizing later doubles the time.

en.title: ND Calculator: Change Filters Without Guessing
en.summary: The ND calculator puts shutter, aperture, ISO, and target exposure in one formula; calculate before swapping.

en.title: Depth of Field Calculator: Distance and Aperture
en.summary: Depth of field starts with subject distance, then aperture and focal length; move and everything changes.

en.title: Bitrate Calculator: How Big Is the File?
en.summary: Calculate file size from minutes and Mbps; know if the drive fits before delivery.

en.title: Budget Calculator: Four Buckets
en.summary: Split the budget into people, gear, location, and post; keep ten percent buffer.

en.title: Subtitle CPS: Can They Read It?
en.summary: Check characters per second; above reading speed, the viewer pauses and the film breaks.

en.title: Aspect Ratio Calculator: Crop and Safe Area
en.summary: Calculate effective pixels after crop, then safe area; vertical is not a horizontal crop.

en.title: Buying a Camera: Budget Before Body
en.summary: On a limited budget, the body is not first. Find whether you lack low light, autofocus, 10-bit, or audio. The wrong body forces every accessory to change with it.

en.title: Renting a Camera: Insurance, Deposit, Check
en.summary: Insurance, deposit, and a hands-on check; film scratches and dead pixels as evidence.

en.title: Buy the Lens First: Focal Length, Aperture, Breathing
en.summary: The lens decides half the image and holds value better than a body. Buy one focal length that covers 70% of your work, then a second; do not start with three cheap zooms.

en.title: Buy Audio First: Mic, Noise Floor, and Gain
en.summary: Audiences forgive a plain image; they do not forgive unclear sound. On a limited budget, put money into a microphone and recorder before a second lens.

en.title: Buying a Light Kit: Soft Before Bright
en.summary: The first light kit is not the brightest; it is the easiest to control skin and shadow. Soft area, consistent color, and dimmability matter more than peak output.

en.title: Buying Project Storage: Speed, Capacity, and Backup
en.summary: Storage is not “bigger is better.” It is “the shoot does not stop, the offload does not lose data, and the project is findable later.” Calculate a real shoot day before buying.

en.title: Buying a Monitor: Brightness, Gamut, and Latency
en.summary: A monitor is not a bigger screen. It must be bright enough outdoors, calibratable, and low-latency for focus; if one fails, the camera screen is better.

en.title: Buying a Tripod: Payload, Torsion, and Height
en.summary: A tripod’s payload rating is not a safety line. Leg stiffness, head lock, torsional rigidity, and centre of gravity decide stability; a flexy tripod rated 20kg still shakes in wind.

en.title: Renting Lighting: List and Damage
en.summary: List, test, and photograph the gear; one missing soft box costs an hour on set.

en.title: Used Gear Check: Shutter, Mount, Sensor
en.summary: Check shutter count, mount play, and sensor dead pixels before paying.

en.title: Overheating Fix: Cool, Segment, Lower Bitrate
en.summary: Cool it, shoot in segments, lower bitrate; do not put a wet towel on the body.

en.title: Jelly Effect Fix: Read Speed and Shutter
en.summary: Rolling shutter comes from slow readout and fast motion; change body or shutter before blaming the lens.

en.title: Audio Noise Fix: Start With the Room
en.summary: Start with the room: air conditioning, lights, outlet, cable; blame the mic last.

en.title: Export Failure Fix: Codec, Disk, Permission
en.summary: Check codec, disk space, and permissions; only then rebuild the project.

en.title: Budget and Quote: Put Risk into the Number
en.summary: A budget is not a cost list; it protects the line that would stop the shoot. A quote is not cost plus 20%; it prices scope, revisions, rights, and risk separately.

en.title: Crew Management: Call Sheet, Sign-In, Wrap, and Ownership
en.summary: Crew management is not sending a call sheet. It makes everyone know the day, the owner of each risk, and when they can leave. Call sheet, sign-in, and wrap report make a project controllable.

en.title: Buying a Cinema Camera: “Can Shoot” Is Not “Can Deliver”
en.summary: A cinema camera’s price is not the body: cards, batteries, monitoring, rig, handles, cables, grading, and learning all count. Confirm the project needs RAW, timecode, SDI, and dual card, or a high-end video body is better value.

en.title: Buying a Zoom: Parfocal, Breathing, and Servo
en.summary: A zoom buys “no lens change,” not “anything.” Confirm it holds focus through the zoom, breathing is controlled, and the servo is quiet; otherwise you bought a prime that can change focal length.

en.title: Field Recorder: Channels, 32-bit Float, and Timecode
en.summary: A field recorder is not about track count. It is about whether one lost channel has a backup, a wrong gain can be saved, and post can sync to timecode.

en.title: Buying LED Lights: Output, Flicker, and Power
en.summary: LED specs are not just wattage. Flicker, color shift, battery runtime, and DMX/wireless control decide whether it works on a real set.

en.title: Buying an HDR Monitor: Peak Nits Is Not Everything
en.summary: HDR monitoring depends on peak, black level, gamut, tone mapping, and calibration. Buying on “1000 nits” alone gets a bright screen with clipped highlights.

en.title: Buying Camera Cards: VPG, Sustained Write, and Heat
en.summary: A card’s peak read speed is irrelevant; sustained write decides whether frames drop. Match the camera’s minimum sustained write, buy one step above, and rotate at least two cards.

en.title: Buying a Fluid Head: Drag, Counterbalance, and Return
en.summary: A fluid head is not “it pans.” The difference is continuous tilt drag, enough counterbalance, and a smooth return when released; these decide whether your pan/tilt is usable.

en.title: Your First Gimbal: Payload, Balance, and Follow
en.summary: A gimbal is not magic for walking. Payload headroom, three-axis balance, follow feel, battery, and axis locks decide whether you can finish a shot.

en.title: Buying Wireless Lavs: Range, Dropouts, and Latency
en.summary: A “500m” wireless lav range is open line-of-sight, not a mall or concert. Test dropouts, noise, latency, and battery in your real scene before choosing.

en.title: Buying Timecode: Drift, Sync, and Battery
en.summary: Timecode is not automatic for multicam, but when needed, drift and sync stability matter more than looks. Test eight-hour drift before deciding how many units.

en.title: Buying NAS/RAID: Throughput, Rebuild, and Noise
en.summary: NAS is not “plug in and safe.” RAID is not backup; rebuilds slow everything, and drive noise/power affect a studio. Calculate throughput and rebuild time first.

en.title: Buying Used Gear: Shutter, Sensor, and Service
en.summary: Used is not “cheap”; it is risk priced in. Check shutter, sensor, ports, and service history before negotiating. Without a test shoot and return terms, walk away.

en.title: Buying Batteries: Capacity, Communication, and Safety
en.summary: A battery is not “it powers on.” Third-party packs may hide percentage, cut out, or swell. On a shoot day, batteries are safety equipment, not a place to save.

en.title: Post Software and Delivery: Workflow Before Tools
en.summary: Editing, grading, audio, encoding and review are five stages. Set the workflow before choosing subscriptions. Do not buy all at once.

en.title: Test Protocol Library: Ten Reproducible On-Set Tests
en.summary: Reproducible steps, raw-data fields and pass lines for ten tests. Without gear, write “not measured”; do not invent numbers.

en.title: Lens Field-of-View Calculator: Focal Length, Sensor, and Horizontal Angle
en.summary: Enter sensor width and focal length to estimate horizontal field of view, and decide whether a lens is wide enough for a room, a landscape, or a close-up.

en.title: Storage chain: card, SSD, NAS and LTO
en.summary: Storage is not one drive; it is a chain from card to work disk, backup and offline media.

en.title: Location sound chain: mic to backup
en.summary: Location sound is not one microphone; it is mic, wireless, recorder, backup and log.

en.title: One-light kit: softbox, reflector, colour
en.summary: One light is enough only when soft area, bounce position and colour temperature agree.

en.title: Camera and lens kit: one body, three lenses
en.summary: The body sets the floor; lenses decide what you can capture. One body and three lenses finish more often.

en.title: Live chain: wireless, monitoring, timecode
en.summary: Live is not camera-to-laptop; wireless, monitoring, timecode and backup are one chain.

en.title: 3-2-1 backup: from card to off-site
en.summary: Backup is not one copy; three copies, two media types and one off-site copy bring footage home.

en.title: Post workstation: NLE, proxies, nodes
en.summary: A workstation is not a spec sheet; NLE, proxies, cache and nodes must not fight in one project.

en.title: AI toolchain: generation, voice, render
en.summary: AI tools are not one-click films; generation, voice, render and human review need a traceable chain.

en.title: Gear Maintenance: Before Call, After Wrap, In Storage
en.summary: Most gear failures are not sudden. They come from long neglect. Make inspection, cleaning, storage and records fixed habits instead of luck.

en.title: Lighting Safety: Power, Heat, Falls, Load
en.summary: Lighting safety is not “be careful”. It is calculating power, heat, falls and load. If any one exceeds the limit, the lamp should not go on.
